literal: Strength which-is-called by-the-goad, the five-all he-who-guards, excellence which-is-called to-the-realm a seed.
translation: He who controls all five senses with the goad of mental strength is a seed for the supreme realm.
modern: மன உறுதி என்னும் அங்குசத்தைக் கொண்டு ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கிக் காப்பவன், மேலான நிலை என்னும் உலகத்திற்கு ஒரு விதை போன்றவன் ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet uses two vivid metaphors to describe the power of self-control. The mind's firmness ('உரன்') is compared to an elephant goad ('தோட்டி') used to master the five senses, which are implicitly likened to wild elephants. A person who guards their senses in this way is described as a seed ('வித்து') planted in the soil or realm of supreme excellence ('வரன் என்னும் வைப்பு'). By calling the ascetic a seed, the poet emphasizes that disciplined self-control is the very origin and potential for ultimate greatness.
